advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have record_criterion_verdict reject (or loudly signal) a criterion_id that is not among the run's minted/expected ids so a mistyped/hallucinated id is not silently banked-and-orphaned.
evidence: completion_banking.py:542 `entry = bank.upsert(criterion_id, met, evidence, source="tool")` — upsert writes any criterion_id with no membership check

completion_banking.py:605 `entry = bank_entries.get(cid)` in assemble_deterministic_verdict and :691 `entry = bank_entries.get(ids[text])` in merge — both key strictly by expected ids, so an unknown-id entry is never read
tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_banking.py:179 `tool("c00-aaaa", True, "e1")` — the tool-contract test banks an arbitrary id with no validation asserted
The tool returns `recorded {criterion_id}` (completion_banking.py:544) confirming a bank that will be orphaned if the id is not an expected minted id
advisory.finding: record_criterion_verdict accepts any criterion_id string with no validation against the expected/minted ids; a hallucinated or mistyped id is written to the bank but downstream consumption (merge_finalizer_with_bank / assemble_deterministic_verdict / _validate_coverage) keys strictly by the expected ids[text], so an orphaned entry is silently ignored and that criterion falls back to a met=false unverified placeholder — defeating the durability goal for the very criterion the model believed it banked.
scenarios: The verifier model transcribes a criterion_id from the manifest with a typo or invents one; the bank records it, the model moves on believing it durable, and on exhaustion that criterion is finalized as an unverified met=false placeholder.
advisory.suggested_fix: Bind the set of valid minted criterion_ids into make_record_tool and, on an unknown id, return an error string naming the valid ids (or raise) rather than upserting it — so the model can correct and re-bank.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish an explicitly-set REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=250 from the unset default (e.g. a dedicated sentinel/flag) so an explicit operator budget is never silently lowered by the criteria-scaled floor.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/completion.py:587: `if cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS or cfg.max_iterations < step_floor:`
src/rebar/llm/config.py:127: `DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS = 250`

Comment claims min-only for explicit budgets (completion.py:552-559: 'min-only against an EXPLICIT operator budget ... only ever raised up to the floor, never lowered'), but the `== DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` branch lowers when the explicit value equals the default sentinel.
REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS maps to max_iterations (src/rebar/llm/config.py:600, docs/llm-framework.md:401 default 250).
advisory.finding: The criteria-scaled primary step-floor detects 'operator set no explicit budget' by the sentinel `cfg.max_iterations == DEFAULT_MAX_ITERATIONS` (250). An operator who EXPLICITLY sets REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS to 250 (equal to the default) is indistinguishable from unset, so their explicit budget is silently LOWERED to the scaled floor (as low as 48 for a small ticket) — contradicting the documented 'an operator who explicitly sets a step budget still wins (min-only)' contract for that one value.
scenarios: An operator pins REBAR_LLM_MAX_STEPS=250 for a completion verify of a small ticket; the run silently executes with a 48-step budget instead of the 250 they requested.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the memo completeness test so a whole-file read that returned exactly _READ_MAX_LINES lines is treated as complete (e.g. mark complete when the whole-file read returned fewer than cap lines OR len(wlines) < cap), rather than `cached_max < cap` which false-negatives at the boundary.
evidence: agent_call.py:227 `entry = {"lines": wlines, "max": cached_max, "complete": cached_max < cap}`
pai_tools.py:63-64 real read_file: `hi = line_end if ... else len(lines); hi = min(hi, lo + _READ_MAX_LINES - 1)` — a 2000-line file with line_end=0 reads all 2000 lines (not truncated)
agent_call.py:209 `_servable` returns entry['complete'] or (le and le <= max); a false 'truncated' at 2000 lines forces the fallback branch for EOF reads
dropped.finding: The read_file memo's 'complete' flag is computed as `cached_max < cap`, which is False for a file with exactly `_READ_MAX_LINES` (2000) lines even though the real read_file returned the whole file. Such a file is treated as truncated, so every subsequent read of it whose line_end is 0 (EOF) or > 2000 fails _servable and falls back to an uncached exact-range tool call — quietly losing the caching benefit precisely at the cap boundary.
scenarios: A file of exactly 2000 lines is read repeatedly at various ranges within one run; every re-read that requests EOF re-executes the wrapped tool, so the 77%-re-read tax lever 2 targets is not collapsed for that file.
